title: Investigate and remediate customer eval drift after runtime sampling/stop-token harmonization
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported reproducible drops in eval pass rates and unexpected truncation of structured outputs after the runtime change that normalized sampling defaults and stop-token handling across environments. Affected customers include two enterprise Dedicated customers (Acme Health, FinLedger) and one Private deployment (GovData). The regression appears to be customer-specific, triggered by a combination of: (1) prompts that relied on implicit stop sequences (newline+delimiter) and (2) downstream eval harnesses that used strict post-processing to detect completion. Root cause hypothesis: the runtime harmonization adjusted the sampling cooling and a minimal post-token filtering step which changed when stop tokens were emitted relative to internal EOS handling. This caused subtle off-by-one token emissions that some evals treat as failures. Impact: production eval pipelines for these customers started failing regression tests (generated answers included residual tokens or missed final punctuation), leading to escalations and feature regressions in paid deployments. Business priority: high due to enterprise SLAs and customer escalations. Goal: ship a transparent fix that preserves prior stop-token semantics for existing customers while exposing controls and tests to prevent future regressions.
activity: 2025-02-18 09:12 - Aisha Kaur: Triage call with support and PM; confirmed three customers reported lowered eval scores after runtime-1.21 rollout. Collected representative prompts, model variants, and exact failure logs.

2025-02-18 13:40 - Miguel Santos: Reproduced failure locally with dockerized runtime-1.21 using Acme Health prompt corpus; observed extra trailing token in ~12% of completions vs runtime-1.20 baseline.

Added fixes and updated tests.

2025-02-22 08:30 - Release Eng: Canary rollout plan drafted: 10% of hosted, 3 Dedicated pools, 2 Private customers with telemetry monitoring for stop-token incidence and eval pass rate. Post-canary gate: 24h stability and no increase in token-level latency.

notes: Decision: preserve historical stop-token emission ordering by default for existing customers on upgrade; new tenants will get harmonized defaults but can opt into legacy semantics via config. This reduces risk of further regressions while allowing us to deprecate legacy behavior after a longer migration period.

Trade-offs: Keeping legacy semantics increases maintenance surface in runtime selection paths; mitigated by adding a clear per-customer config and automated test coverage. Long-term plan is to document differences and provide migration tooling to validate prompt/eval suites against the harmonized behavior.

Follow-ups: Add monitoring that alerts when stop-token divergence rate exceeds 0.5% for a customer, expand unit tests to cover batched stop sequences, and provide customers an exportable 'golden' evaluator to validate against runtime upgrades.
Customer communications: Drafted postmortem + proposed timeline for full rollout to be reviewed by Customer Success before sending to impacted customers.
